source_snapshot.procedure_direct_xlsx: 【Before Test】 1. Check that the SUT configuration (e.g., hardware, firmware, drivers, etc.) matches the specifications/recipe definition. 2. Clear logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.). 3. The following BIOS settings paths are from the Intel reference platform. Locations of these settings may be different on your BIOS implementation Customer Scripts (CScripts) Enabling The following is a quick reference of the key BIOS knobs for CScripts: • EDKII > Socket Configuration > Processor Configuration > Lock Chipset = Disable • EDKII > Socket Configuration > Processor Configuration > MSR Lock Control = Disable • EDKII > Socket Configuration > IIO Configuration > DFX Global Configuration > — EV DFX Features = Enable — Disable BIOS Done = [X] ELOG Enabling • EDKII > Platform Configuration > System Event Log > eMCA Settings > — EMCA Error Support= Enable — EMCA Logging Support= Enable — Corrected Error eLog = Enable — Memory Error eLog = Enable — Processor Error eLog = Enable Error Reporting Enabling • EDKII > Platform Configuration > System Event Log > WHEA Settings > — WHEA Support = Enable — WHEA Log Memory Error = Enable — WHEA Log Processor Error = Enable — WHEA Log PCI Error = Enable Error Injection Enabling • EDKII > Platform Configuration > System Event Log > — System Errors = Enable — System Memory Poison = Enable • EDKII > Platform Configuration > System Event Log > Error Injection Settings > — MCA Bank Error Injection Support = Enable — WHEA Error Injection Support = Enable — WHEA PCIe* Error Injection Support = Enable — WHEA PCIe* Error Action Table = Enable • EDKII > Platform Configuration > System Event Log > IIO Error Enabling > — IIO/PCH Global Error Support = Enable — IIO MCA Support = Disable — IIO eDPC Support = Disable • EDKII > Platform Configuration > System Event Log > PCIE Error Enabling > PCIe* Corrected Error Threshold Counter = Disable • EDKII > Platform Configuration > System Event Log > PCIE Error Enabling > PCIe AER Corrected Errors = Enable • EDKII > Platform Configuration > System Event Log > EMCA Settings > LMCE Support = Enable • EDKII > Platform Configuration > System Event Log > Memory Error Enabling > Memory Corrected Error = Enable • EDKII > Socket Configuration > Uncore Configuration > Uncore General Configuration > Directory Mode Enable = Disable • EDKII > Platform Configuration > Miscellaneous Configuration > Enable DAM Pin = Enable Firmware First Model • EDKII > Platform Configuration > System Event Log > EMCA Settings > — EMCA Logging Support = Enable — EMCA CMCI-SMI Morphing = EMCA gen2 CSMI — EMCA CMCI-SMI Threshold = 0 — EMCA MCA-SMI Enable = EMCA gen 2 - MSMI • EDKII > Platform Configuration > System Event Log > IIO Error Enabling > OS Native AER Support = Disable Crash Log • EDKII > Platform Configuration > System Event Log > Crash Log Enabling > CPU CrashLog Feature = Disable • EDKII > Platform Configuration > System Event Log > Crash Log Enabling > PCH CrashLog Feature = Disable 4. Other OS Notes You can use grub2-mkconfig to specify "ras=cec_disable" by modifying /etc/default/grub's "GRUB_CMDLINE_LINUX" with "ras=cec_disable". 【During Test】 1. Specific BIOS setup : • EDKII > Platform Configuration > System Event Log > Memory Error Enabling > — Spare Interrupt = SMI • EDKII > Socket Configuration > Memory Configuration > Memory RAS Configuration > — Correctable Error Threshold = 2 — Trigger SW Error Threshold= Disabled — ADDDC Sparing = Enable • Socket Configuration > Memory Configuration > — Enforce Population POR = Disable • Disabling this knob is not required but was disabled because a non-POR memory population was used to create this recipe. It is recommended to have a POR memory population. 2. Establish 1 bank VLS region as described in One Bank VLS Region. 3. Halt the system for error injections. >>> halt() 4. The hardware per rank CECC error thresholds were set to "2" so inject two CECC errors to a different device and bank compared to the location/target in step 1. >>> ei.mem.memDevs(dev0=1, dev0msk=0x3, dev1=1, dev1msk=0x0) >>> ei.mem.injectMemError(socket=0, channel=0, dimm=0, rank=0, sub_channel=0, bank_group=0, bank=1, errType="ce", verbose=True, sub_rank=0, ps_ch=0, showErrorRegs=True, checkEInjLock=False) >>> ei.mem.memDevs(dev0=1, dev0msk=0x3, dev1=1, dev1msk=0x0) >>> ei.mem.injectMemError(socket=0, channel=0, dimm=0, rank=0, sub_channel=0, bank_group=0, bank=1, errType="ce", verbose=True, sub_rank=0, ps_ch=0, showErrorRegs=True, checkEInjLock=False) 5. Check that the per rank CECC error threshold has been met. >>> ras.mem.adddc_status_check(socket=0, mc=0) 6. Resume the system so BIOS can perform its SMM flow. >>> go() 7. Expecting VLS sparing operations to occur to create a 2nd bank VLS region so copy_in_progress should be 1. >>> sv.socket0.compute0.uncore.memss.mc0.ch0.mcchan.sparing_patrol_status.show() 8. Verify that the initial bank VLS region remains the same, there's a 2nd bank VLS region which aligns with expectations, and the per rank CECC error counter was cleared. >>> ras.mem.adddc_status_check(socket=0, mc=0)

test_case.purpose: Verify ADDDC allocates a second bank-VLS region when a failed rank already has one bank region and reaches threshold on another device in another bank, while preserving the original region.
required_package: GNR/BIOS/BMC/OS, DIMM topology and POR/non-POR disposition
Initial bank-VLS device/bank/rank plus proof dev0=1 bank1 differs on both axes
Expected second-region failed/buddy mapping and counter-clear oracle
SMM completion timeout, serial/OOB recovery and restoration plan
test_case.test_command: Capture source RAS settings and exact initial VLS region; halt; prove dev0=1/bank1 differs from predecessor device/bank; set mask0x3 and inject exactly two CEs at source coordinates; verify threshold; go once; optionally observe copy_in_progress=1; compare ADDDC status to prove original region unchanged, correctly mapped second bank region present and per-rank counter cleared; restore and verify health.
